title: Adaptive SLI Guardrails and Initiative Burn Rebalancer
creator: Marisol Chen
description: Problem: Teams struggle to translate organization-level SLI targets and error-budget allocations into per-initiative rollout gates and oncall actions. We often see either overly conservative holds that block important experiments or permissive rollouts that exhaust error budgets and trigger late firefighting. Goal: deliver a first-class tracking-and-action flow that (1) maps SLI targets to initiative-level budgets, (2) provides adaptive guardrails that automatically tighten or relax rollout gates based on short-term burn and long-term runway, and (3) surfaces actionable remediation suggestions for oncall and PMs in the Console. This ticket ships the product design, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the "Burn Rebalancer" feature and the SLI Guardrails UI components.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows per-initiative SLI target, allocated error budget, current burn rate, and projected runway (24h/7d) for any initiative with an active rollout
Automated guardrail policy engine can block or throttle canary/percent-rollouts when projected runway < configured threshold and records the decision in the initiative timeline
Rebalancer suggests transfer actions when aggregate error-budget pool has uneven consumption (UI and CSV export) and allows PM approval to execute reallocation
Oncall runbook card populates with prioritized remediation steps based on failure mode taxonomy and links to relevant dashboards and PRs
Telemetry: new metrics emitted (initiative.burn_rate, initiative.runway_hours, guardrail.decision) and dashboards created in Grafana for cross-team visibility
Feature flags enable staged rollout: internal-only -> opt-in teams -> org-wide, with clear rollback knobs

updates: 2026-02-24 - Marisol Chen: Kickoff meeting with Reliability and Console leads. Agreed on primary telemetry sources: per-route SLI windows (p50/p95/p99), error classifications, and rollout percentages from Router service.

2026-03-02 - Arjun Patel: Policy DSL landed in branch feature/guardrails-dsl. Early decision to express guardrails as 'runway_hours' thresholds rather than absolute error counts to normalize across traffic volume.

2026-03-08 - SRE feedback (Lena Morales): Prefer conservative default for first 72h; recommend automatic alerting to oncall instead of automatic block for non-critical initiatives. Marked as trade-off in design doc.
2026-03-11 - Engineering (ENG-4281): API v1 endpoints merged; added initiative.burn_rate and initiative.runway_hours metrics. Instrumentation tests added to CI.
2026-03-12 - PM note: Scheduled pilot with Search and Console teams for 2026-04-05. Drafted communication for opt-in teams outlining expected behaviors and rollback steps.
2026-03-14 - Design review: UI card prototypes validated; UX asked to show both short-term (24h) and trend (7d) runways side-by-side. Implementing in UI alpha.

Open question: How should we handle cross-initiative dependencies when rebalancer suggests moving budget from one initiative to another? Proposed: require explicit PM approval and write audit log entry.
notes: Trade-offs: automatic enforcement reduces manual toil but risks blocking experiments; plan to neutralize risk with feature flags and conservative defaults.
Edge cases: traffic spikes from synthetic tests can distort runway; will add filtering for synthetic-origin tags and apply smoothing window of 30m by default.
Localization: UI strings need translation — added i18n label to backlog for Cycle 12.
Rollout: start internal teams then open opt-in; require opt-in teams to provide a contact and expected traffic profile for pilot acceptance.
